items.title: Second-stage authoring throughput proof

priority.rationale: Mandatory before P3 content scale.

acceptance.acceptanceRule: Before the first comparable P1-C execution/runtime mutation, freeze AUTHORING-LEDGER-01, THROUGHPUT-COMPARISON-01, the matched scope fingerprint, measurement endpoint, exclusions, immutable opening-receipt schema, and a product-approved material-improvement threshold. Static P1-B Station Add identity/anchor/payload authoring is outside the prospective clock; prior P1-B effort is RetrospectiveUnavailable, and reconstructed estimates may describe history but cannot serve as the comparison baseline or support an improvement claim.

Before the first comparable P1-C execution/runtime mutation, seal an immutable opening receipt containing ledger ID/schema, start-manifest digest, scope fingerprint, start timestamp, contributor set, exclusions, and threshold; then use the same AUTHORING-LEDGER-01 schema later used for the second stage. Pass only after accepted P1-C and an exact endpoint manifest containing content truth, relevant validator, focused runtime, route/result regressions, and continuous-gate evidence. P2-B is not part of this first-pocket baseline, the first validator PASS is not the endpoint, and a reconstructed or late-opened ledger cannot pass.

After P1-B truthful joins, accepted P1-C/P2-B, and the first-pocket ledger, freeze exactly one EXPANSION-CANDIDATE-LEDGER-01 row with a distinct contentPromiseId/revision, fresh six-axis PRODUCT-DECISION-V1 score and rationale, scope fingerprint, logical route/condition contract, catalog-generation transition, physical host choice, foundation/content/stabilization accounting boundary, explicit inclusions/exclusions, and exact acceptance/evidence plan. Passing this row authorizes no implementation, source mutation, runtime owner, P3 family, or inherited score.

Delivery-only gate: implement and verify exactly the candidate contract already frozen by ACC-OPS-SECOND-STAGE-CANDIDATE-CONTRACT-FROZEN as one short distinct logical stage. It must reuse the route spine, run/result, encounter bridge, presentation lifecycle, and validators without a new scene-specific route manager; contract selection, score changes, scope expansion, or candidate substitution cannot pass this gate.

Before the first in-scope second-stage mutation, seal an immutable opening receipt containing ledger ID/schema, candidate/start-manifest digest, matched scope fingerprint, start timestamp, contributor set, exclusions, and threshold. Use the same AUTHORING-LEDGER-01 schema and matched measurement endpoint as the first pocket; record exact source/scope manifests, active/tool-wait/excluded person-time, manual and generated edits, stable defect lifecycle rows, eligible reuse denominator/dispositions, foundation/content/stabilization effort, and derived metrics through the accepted endpoint. A reconstructed or late-opened ledger cannot pass, and a measured second-stage baseline is not itself a throughput-improvement result.

The second stage is a distinct logical playableStageId, route revision/digest, and contentPromiseId/revision, not a catalog alias, renamed encounter, difficulty-only variation, or another physical segment. It owns a truthful template/briefing, meaningful executable content delta and encounter binding, exact catalog projection, its own StageProgressionNode/Graph identity and directed edge, result definition and result/progression sidecar, and an admission-time deep-copied join snapshot whose current-run presentation is invariant to later authoring mutation. Its committed summary must not reuse Olympus identity/facts, and its Clear/Fail plus Replay/Retry/Lobby routes must return Replay/Retry to its own exact entry stage. NEW-LIGHTWEIGHT-SCENE must prove exact definition/build route with no duplicate run manager/direct load; ROUTE-SELECTED-SHARED-HOST must prove route-selected definition/encounter/fact/presentation, zero Olympus-adapter leakage, and zero stale configuration after replay. Existing managers and validators remain the sole reusable owners.

Apply frozen THROUGHPUT-COMPARISON-01 to the exact first-pocket and second-stage ledgers. Pass only when matched-scope active person-time meets the preregistered material-improvement threshold, every mandated shared route/run-result/encounter/presentation/validator capability is reused, newSceneSpecificOwnerCount is zero, manual scene edits and blocking-defect counts do not increase, content-truth and continuous gates pass, and the reviewer accepts the comparison. Baseline-only, retrospective, scope-drifted, or otherwise incomparable ledgers cannot pass or promote P3.

priority.rationale: Required before external support or release operations.

Stable semantic string IDs pass missing/duplicate-key, pseudo-locale, overflow, and supported-resolution checks without making localized copy a gameplay identity.

For every admitted UI surface, readableLabelKey, narrationKey, focusOrder, minimumFontSize, contrastClass, and requiresInputPrompt each receive Executed or explicit Unsupported disposition. The first bounded proof covers StageSelect Start/Back consumers, focus traversal, font size, input prompt, safe-area, pseudo-locale, and supported-resolution behavior; authored-only narration or contrast cannot count as runtime proof.

A versioned support bundle contains only sealed IDs/digests, build/config hash, typed fault codes, and redacted environment class; redaction tests forbid raw identifiers, input, free text, and mutable screenshots/logs as truth.
One synthetic resolver/load/unload or persistence fault follows the named severity, owner, and escalation path, preserves canonical gameplay truth, and records recovery and closure evidence.

items.title: Staged release and rollback operations

priority.rationale: Final operations-track gate after product demand and readiness.

roadmapRefs: SUBCULTURE_DATASET_GAP_ROADMAP.md::P3 — Broaden content operations only after repeat play works
items.resumeCondition: Repeat-play demand, persistence/migration, QA/localization/support, deployment, privacy, and rollback prerequisites are all accepted.

acceptance.acceptanceRule: A hash-addressed previous/current release manifest and staged activation receipt drive an injected-failure rollback drill. The manifest binds each content-bundle digest, compatible app/schema range, activation cohort, in-flight-run policy, rollback target, and cache-invalidation receipt. Rollback invalidates pending loads/callbacks, restores the prior compatible content/config route, preserves durable progress under the documented rollback-read boundary, and passes the canonical route plus current build checks without inventing or duplicating settlement.

Name the release owner and on-call boundary; produce a schema-compatible manifest containing exact app/package, content-bundle, config, store-schema, route/catalog, activation-cohort, in-flight-run, and rollback-target identities; and admit only an explicitly privacy-approved aggregate metric inventory tied to the measured demand source. externalSinkDisposition remains TypedAbsent; approving metric names is not approval to transmit them.

One releaseCandidateSnapshotRefId and releaseManifestDigest contain readinessCoverage rows for build manifest and Android performance, diagnostics/privacy, QA/localization/accessibility/support/incident, P1-D migration/backup rollback-read, P2-C store migration, second-stage truth/throughput, and the bounded P3 slice. Each row names acceptanceId, proofRefId, coveredManifestDigest, and FreshPass or CoveredHashesUnchanged; stale item status alone cannot satisfy release readiness.

nextAction.description: Do not create a release train or metrics inventory before every resume condition is met.

rejections.negativeBoundary: Do not copy proprietary assets, code, formulas, dialogue, stage layouts, UI art, animation, audiovisual content, opaque numeric meanings, or score/economy rules.
Do not promote stamina, random drops, shops, gacha/equipment breadth, roguelike affix graphs, daily/liveops shells, or generic ranking before the P3 demand gate.
Never reinterpret current NotAdmitted/zero-pending rows as future admitted-owner success or quiescence.

validationRules: Every itemId is unique.
Every parentId and dependency itemId resolves.
The dependency graph is acyclic.
Every evidenceRefId and source claim ID resolves.
Every promotionGate acceptance ID resolves within its item.
Every required non-pass acceptance row carries an acceptanceRule, predicate, or at least one resolvable acceptanceContractRef; an ID and prose-only item link are insufficient.

Every acceptanceDependencies itemId resolves; a non-null acceptanceId resolves within that exact item, the combined item/acceptance dependency graph is acyclic, and the dependent acceptance cannot pass until the declared accepted/pass state is satisfied. An acceptance dependency does not block measurement or preparation of independent sibling rows.
Every continuousPromotionGateRef resolves to a global gate, and every backing item and backing acceptance ID declared by a global gate resolves.

An item with continuousPromotionGateRefs cannot transition to accepted unless every applicable required arm of every referenced gate is satisfied by evidence from the same named immutable source/configuration snapshot as that item's promotion evidence; historical evidence from an earlier snapshot is insufficient.
A partial item may retain verified subgate passes while a continuous gate remains open, but no such pass promotes the item to accepted.
Accepted items have no required non-pass acceptance row.
Partial items have at least one required pass row and at least one required non-pass row.
Hold items declare resumeCondition.
Product and evidence score profiles are never merged.
Every item appears in exactly one priority track; sequence values are compared only inside that track.
Sequence values are unique and continuous within each priority track.
The global topological order contains every item exactly once and places every dependency before its consumer.

P3-RELEASE-OPS requires accepted P3 content and OPS-P2 readiness plus ACC-P3-RELEASE-CANDIDATE-READINESS-COVERAGE from the exact candidate snapshot; that coverage must bind fresh or hash-unchanged evidence for P1-D/P2-C persistence, build/perf, diagnostics/privacy, throughput/content truth, QA/localization/accessibility/support/incident, and the bounded P3 slice.
Every PRODUCT-DECISION-V1 score provides all six dimensions and an arithmetic total; items with incomplete dimensions use scoreProfileId null rather than a product score.
Every scoreAsOfSnapshotRefId resolves to snapshotRefs, and its effectiveScope prevents a partial subgate score from being presented as the remaining or completed scope alone.
Analysis packet order never overrides product dependency order.
